design.md's SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate contradicts requirements.md AC-015's and AC-028's own hard-failure trigger language, and design.md's round-2 reconciliation subsection ('Relationship to requirements.md's own SKIP language') addresses only AC-006's softer 'until Epic A1 merges' phrasing. It never mentions AC-015's separate sentence -- 'a SKIP surviving validate-live-host-proof after Epic A1 merges is a non-zero-exit hard failure, never a passing state' (requirements.md:389) -- nor AC-028's parallel 'reports a non-zero exit on any missing, SKIP-after-merge, FAIL, stale ... record' (requirements.md:536). Both state a single-clause trigger: merge alone converts a surviving SKIP into a hard failure. design.md's mechanism is a two-clause predicate requiring BOTH that the owning task has started AND that the artifacts exist on main, and design.md says so in direct opposition to that text: 'never merely until Epic A1 merges'; 'a case can stay a valid, non-failing SKIP for a period after Epic A1 actually merges, for as long as its own owning task has not yet started'; and the Risks section's 'AC-006/AC-015/AC-016 can each remain a valid, non-failing SKIP for an unbounded period after Epic A1's own canonical artifacts actually land on main'. security-spec.md's B3 boundary and STRIDE row state the identical trade-off by name against AC-006, AC-015, AC-016. validate-live-host-proof's contract reports exit 0 'pending' for a pre-activation SKIP regardless of Epic A1's merge state -- the literal behavior AC-015/AC-028 say must be a non-zero-exit hard failure once Epic A1 has merged. requirements.md, acceptance-tests.md and tasks.md are frozen for this round, so this is an unresolved contradiction rather than a stale artifact. Concrete failure mode: a Phase 2/3 implementer or CI cannot determine from the normative documents whether a still-present SKIP after Epic A1 merges is a passing or failing state for AC-015/AC-028 -- the two documents give opposite answers for the same event.

No performance requirements found in requirements.md. This is an internal test-infrastructure specification with no response-time/throughput/latency/SLA statement; the closest numeric threshold (nonce 24-hour TTL) is a replay control, not a performance requirement.

design.md's Data Plan states no migration is required because every data entity is a net-new file with no prior version. The one write against pre-existing data (marking consumed_by_record on an existing nonce-ledger entry) is explicitly characterized as additive metadata, not a schema migration.

Every REQ-001..REQ-007 goal maps to a design.md component/section, and design.md's Layer Specifications and Cross-Layer Dependencies sections cite requirements.md's Non-goals to bound scope. No component, schema or endpoint in design.md lacks a corresponding AC; ADR-0028 implements AC-026's already-stated two-party-attestation requirement rather than introducing new scope.
